title: The fire taught and repeated
theme: Death teaches the fire, the first of the worlds — which bricks, how many, how laid — and Naciketas repeats it back; Death, pleased, speaks again.

sandhi.rule: Final m stays before a vowel.
The visarga of -āḥ is lost before a vowel: P. 8.3.17 (भोभगोअघोअपूर्वस्य योऽशि) with P. 8.3.19 (लोपः शाकल्यस्य).

sandhi.type: āḥ before a voiced consonant; īḥ before v
sandhi.rule: āḥ loses its visarga before a voiced consonant, P. 8.3.22 (हलि सर्वेषाम्); after ī the visarga becomes r.
Final t before y becomes d, P. 8.2.39 (झलां जशोऽन्ते); m before a vowel stays; a + a → ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः).
punar keeps its r before a vowel; a + ā → ā, P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः).

morphology.note: Nominative plural feminine of yāvat; classical yāvatyaḥ. Raṅgarāmānuja: a Vedic pūrvasavarṇa form, «पूर्वसवर्णः छान्दसः».
The perfect of ah ‘say’, used with present or past sense.

translation.literal: ‘He told him that fire, the beginning of the worlds — which bricks, how many, or how [laid]. And he too repeated it back as it was told. Then Death, pleased at him, spoke again.’
translation.readable: ‘So Death taught him the fire that is the origin of the worlds — what bricks it takes, how many, and how they are laid. Naciketas repeated it back exactly. Pleased, Death spoke again.’

syntax: The first half is narrative: Death told him the fire, with an indirect list of what was taught (yā iṣṭakā yāvatīr vā yathā vā — which bricks, how many, how). The second: Naciketas repeated it; Death, pleased, spoke again. Śaṅkara notes that the voice is now the text’s own, not Yama’s: «इदं श्रुतेर्वचनम्».

ambiguities.topic: lokādi: ‘first of the worlds’ in what sense?
ambiguities.note: Śaṅkara: the fire is the first of the worlds because it was the first embodied being (Virāj): «लोकानामादिं प्रथमशरीरित्वात्». Raṅgarāmānuja: the cause of the world reached, i.e. leading to heaven: «लोकस्य आदिम् – हेतुम्; स्वर्ग्यमिति यावत्».
GRETIL and Madhva’s text read punar āha without eva; the base, the vishvAsa mūla and Śaṅkara read punar evāha (corrections.json).

metre.name: triṣṭubh
metre.note: Counted as written, 22 and 23 syllables; the second line is one syllable long (sa cāpi tat pratyavadad yathoktam athāsya mṛtyuḥ punar evāha tuṣṭaḥ). Without eva, as GRETIL and Madhva read, it would have 22 — a metrical argument some editors use for that reading; the edition keeps the base text.

beginner: This verse is told by the Upaniṣad itself, not by Yama or Naciketas. Death teaches the boy the fire ritual in detail: which bricks are used, how many, and how they are laid. The Upaniṣad does not repeat the details; it only says they were taught. Then Naciketas repeats everything back exactly, as a good student in the Vedic schools would. Death is pleased with him. The verse shows the old way of learning by careful listening and exact repetition, and it shows a teacher’s delight in a student who has truly taken in the lesson.
analogy: Like a music teacher who plays a passage once, hears the student play it back without a single slip, and smiles.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Death teaches the fire — bricks, number, method; Naciketas repeats it exactly; Death, pleased, speaks again (the next verses).

commentary.q: Why are the details not given?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The Upaniṣad states that the bricks, their number and their method were taught, without giving them. Śaṅkara: «याः इष्टकाः चेतव्याः स्वरूपेण यावतीर्वा सङ्ख्यया यथा वा चीयतेऽग्निर्येन प्रकारेण सर्वमेतदुक्तवानित्यर्थः». Raṅgarāmānuja says the same: «यल्लक्षणाः इष्टकाश्चेतव्याः, यत्संख्याकाः, येन प्रकारेण चेतव्याः».

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Śaṅkara: pleased by the student’s exact repetition, Death wants to give a further boon besides the three: «अथ अस्य प्रत्युच्चारणेन तुष्टः सन् मृत्युः पुनरेवाह वरत्रयव्यतिरेकेणान्यं वरं दित्सुः». Raṅgarāmānuja: «शिष्यस्य ग्रहणसामर्थ्यदर्शनेन सन्तुष्टस्सन्».

advaita.text: The fire is ‘first of the worlds’ as Virāj, the first embodied being: «लोकानामादिं प्रथमशरीरित्वात्». The verse is narrative; its teaching is the student’s exact reception.

visistadvaita.text: The fire is the cause of reaching that world: «लोकस्य आदिम् – हेतुम्; स्वर्ग्यमिति यावत्». The student’s capacity to grasp is what pleases the teacher.

schools.disagreement: Only on lokādi: Śaṅkara’s ‘first embodied being’ against Raṅgarāmānuja’s ‘cause of [reaching] the world’. Madhva has no separate comment on this verse in the imported text.

contemporary.text: Repeating a lesson back exactly is an old method, and still a good test of listening: it shows what was actually heard. The teacher’s pleasure here is the pleasure of being understood. (A modern reflection.)

reflect.beginner: When did someone last understand you exactly as you meant?
reflect.deeper: Why might exact repetition be the first step to understanding, not the last?
reflect.practice: In your next conversation, repeat back the other person’s main point in their words before answering.

references.text: Madhva has no separate comment on this mantra in the imported text.

flags.note: punar evāha (base, vishvAsa mūla, Śaṅkara) against punar āha (GRETIL, Madhva, Raṅgarāmānuja’s text); the shorter reading regularises the metre.
